text:
He should be found guilty of battery. His admitted indifference to the consequences of reckless driving is a conscious disregard of a substantial risk, which satisfies the general-intent mens rea for criminal battery even though he had no purpose to injure anyone. Attempted manslaughter does not fit, because attempt requires a specific intent to commit the crime and involuntary manslaughter is not a specific-intent offense.

CONFIDENCE: 88
